ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of subscribers, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, counterparties, merchants, and payment-rail partners against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, APG/FATF public statements, and the domestic FIU list under the AML/CFT Act 2022; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all Politically Exposed Persons and for corporate subscribers requiring beneficial-ownership look-through prior to incorporation and license filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Registrar of International Companies, Apia, Samoa, statutory e-Services name reservation and filing portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be expressed in Latin (Roman) alphabetic script; Samoan-language names are permitted using standard Samoan orthography, but the English name governs for International Companies; non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese characters) are not accepted as the registered name but may be adopted as transliterated trading or foreign names; the statutory name must terminate with 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation and must be distinguishable from all existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30-day period upon written application to SIFA and payment of the prescribed search and extension fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a formal objection with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, user consent letters, or prior approvals from the Central Bank of Samoa for financial and banking tokens; if the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days under the International Companies Act 1987-88; in parallel, a revised name may be resubmitted through the SIFA portal after payment of a fresh reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual or mail-forwarding office is not permissible as the sole commercial substance for this licensed high-risk lender. The International Companies Act 1987-88 requires a registered office in Samoa maintained by a licensed registered agent; Central Bank of Samoa licensing for micro-lending and P2P platforms additionally requires a physical Apia office with locally resident compliance and money-laundering reporting officers. A virtual office may supplement but cannot replace the required physical presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 65-70% probability of an unannounced or short-notice physical inspection within the first 12 months of licensing, reflecting Central Bank of Samoa on-site examination powers and SIFA registered-agent inspection cycles.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 50 (incorporation, constitution, registered office, registered agent and first directors); Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa) for AML registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form IC-1) together with the Memorandum of Association (Charter), Articles of Association, and Statement of Compliance
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the International Companies Act 1987; capital may be expressed in any currency; no escrow or deposit account requirement at incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The share capital as stated in the Statement of Application is subscribed for and the directors shall issue the allotted shares to the subscribers upon payment of the subscription moneys. (2) The registered office of the Company shall be established at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and the agent is engaged as registered agent. (3) The persons designated in the application are confirmed as first directors, and the corporate secretary and such officers as recorded in the minutes are appointed. (4) Each director is authorized to open bank accounts, engage auditors, and execute all documents incident to incorporation. (5) These resolutions take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-Name (name reservation) to the SIFA Registry through the licensed registered agent or via the SIFA e-services portal. The proposed name must end with 'International Company', 'Corporation', 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. If the name contains restricted financial terms such as 'Lending', 'Finance' or 'Bank', obtain a written no-objection from the Central Bank of Samoa before reservation.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport copy of the beneficial owner and subscriber
Central Bank of Samoa no-objection letter (for restricted financial words)
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as similar or objectionable, the applicant may within 14 days file a written appeal to the Registrar; in practice counsel submits two alternative names and the reservation is re-run. Any Central Bank restriction letter is cured by obtaining conditional authorization from the Central Bank of Samoa before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent and Notary Public in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association (Charter) and Articles of Association in accordance with sections 6 to 9 of the International Companies Act 1987. Subscribers execute the Charter and Articles before a notary public, and the registered agent certifies the Statement of Compliance. All documents must be in English and contain the company name, registered office, authorised share capital, and particulars of first directors.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association (Charter)
Articles of Association
Subscriber statement and consent to act as director
Registered agent's certified Statement of Compliance
Declaration of non-resident ownership and tax-exempt status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or agent queries incomplete subscriber details, correct the relevant schedule and re-execute the document; a fresh notarial certificate is attached while the original date is preserved where the defect is purely formal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Registrar and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1 together with the executed Charter, Articles, Statement of Compliance, consents of directors and registered office confirmation to the SIFA Registry through the licensed registered agent. Pay the official incorporation fee of USD 250 by bank transfer to the SIFA prescribed account. Upon verification of completeness, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation
Charter and Articles of Association (executed and notarized)
Statement of Compliance
Notice of first directors and registered office
Official fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries completeness, the applicant may cure within 21 days by filing an amending letter; a substantial amendment is re-dated by the Registrar but does not invalidate incorporation. A certified copy of any correction is then recorded in the Register of International Companies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company, recorded with the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the statutory first board meeting or adopt a written circular resolution signed by all directors, approving the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. Record the minutes, issue share certificates to the subscribers, and maintain the register of members, officers and registered office address in the Company's statutory records held by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (signed)
Minutes of first board meeting
Register of members and share certificates
Consents of appointed officers
Registered office address confirmation letter from the agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum cannot be achieved in person, a written resolution signed by each director is valid under the International Companies Act 1987; if any officer declines appointment, a supplementary resolution is passed and re-filed with the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Samoa, Financial Supervision Department; Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Central Bank of Samoa for the Lender's Licence (micro-credit and peer-to-peer digital lending) under the Lending Act 2008. File the application with the Financial Supervision Department together with the Certificate of Incorporation, AML/CFT manual, borrower and investor terms, payment outsourcing arrangements with ACH and local wallet providers, and fit-and-proper declarations. Concurrently register with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit as a financial service provider under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. The licence imposes platform-specific conditions on transaction monitoring, borrower caps and reporting.
required_dossiers: Lender's Licence application form
Business plan for the P2P micro-lending platform
AML/CFT policy and procedures manual
Fit-and-proper declarations of directors and shareholders
Certificate of Incorporation, Charter and Articles
Outsourcing agreements with payment rails (ACH_Direct_Debit and Local_Wallet_Payout)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused or conditioned, the applicant may respond to the Central Bank's proposed action notice within 21 days and may appeal to the Minister of Finance under section 21 of the Lending Act 2008. Additional anti-money-laundering documentation may be filed with the Financial Intelligence Unit to expedite registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Business Licence and Occupational and Fire Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licensing Division; Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the Apia administrative office, obtain the Annual Business Licence from MCIL by submitting incorporation records, lease details and the insurance policy. Secure a Fire Safety Clearance from FESA for the office premises following inspection of fire exits, extinguishers and alarm systems. Because the International Company is a tax-exempt offshore entity, no domestic income tax or GST registration is required; the MCIL licence is issued only for physical presence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
SIFA confirmation of tax-exempt status
Annual Business Licence application form
Lease agreement for the Apia office premises
FESA inspection report and fire safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MCIL questions the offshore status, provide the SIFA no-objection certificate confirming that the International Company may conduct regulated lending activities outside the domestic market. Any fire safety deficits are remediated by installing the required equipment and requesting a re-inspection within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Central Bank of Samoa, Financial Supervision Department, and Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for offshore financial services licensing; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for physical office licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Lender's Licence (micro-credit and peer-to-peer lending platform) under the Lending Act 2008 (Samoa) and AML registration as a Financial Service Provider under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - administrative and office-based fintech operations with no manufacturing discharge; minor office fit-out may require a Development Consent registration under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 (Samoa)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or industrial discharge permitted; compliance with MNRE ambient noise and air quality standards for any backup generator; electronic waste and battery disposal must follow the Waste Management Act 2005 (Samoa); office water discharge must meet the Samoa National Effluent Standards if a septic system is installed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire and Emergency Services Act 2014 (Samoa) issued by FESA for the Apia office; structural occupancy clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure; occupational health and safety clearance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 (Samoa) and worker's compensation registration with the Accident Compensation Corporation of Samoa.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa (integrated customs and inland revenue administration); e-services are accessed through the MfR Tax Online Portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An offshore International Company (IC) is first incorporated under the International Companies Act 1988 (as amended) through a licensed registered agent, with the Registrar of International Companies operating under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour. The IC is issued a Certificate of Exemption and is not required to register for income tax or VAGST with the Ministry for Revenue (MfR) so long as it does not transact business with Samoan residents or derive Samoan-source income. If the IC subsequently hires Samoan-resident employees, owns land in Samoa, or undertakes any other domestic taxable activity, it must apply to the MfR for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) within 14 days after becoming liable, using the prescribed application form, corporate constitutional documents, directors' and registered agent's identification, and evidence of incorporation; the TIN is issued by the MfR and is also a prerequisite for customs clearance if import transactions arise. An exempt IC must, in all cases, maintain its registered office and registered agent in Samoa and discharge the annual economic substance notification obligation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the International Company is treated as a Samoan offshore exempt entity: it is not resident for income tax on foreign-source business receipts, is not liable to VAGST on offshore financial supplies, and is exempt from stamp duty and exchange control, subject to the statutory limitations on carrying on business in or with Samoa and to the OECD-compliant economic substance requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity election. The exempt classification is mandatory for International Companies and cannot be waived or selectively opted out of; the IC may, however, request a binding tax ruling from the MfR confirming that a specified activity remains offshore-source and exempt. The Income Tax Act 2012 and the Tax Administration Act 2016 contain general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR), and Samoa applies internationally aligned hybrid mismatch and CFC ordering rules for resident companies; no elective hybrid-mismatch regime is available to exempt ICs, and double tax treaty relief does not apply to the IC's offshore income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAGST registration applies when taxable supplies, excluding exempt financial supplies, exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed WST 75,000 in any 12-month period; a person making only exempt supplies is not registrable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has not introduced mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal digital stamping, or government API clearance. VAGST-registered businesses must issue a VAT invoice containing all prescribed particulars (supplier name and TIN, recipient details, description of supply, consideration, and VAGST amount) and retain original records for at least 7 years; returns and schedules are filed electronically through the MfR portal. Electronically generated invoices and optional QR codes are accepted, but there is no statutory fiscal clearance or digital sealing mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a supply of goods is zero-rated where the goods are exported from Samoa within 28 days after the supply, title passes to a non-resident customer, and the supplier retains documentary evidence of physical export. Services: an offshore supply of services is zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident acting outside Samoa and the services are not used or enjoyed in Samoa. For the P2P micro-lending platform, loan interest and loan-origination or intermediation services are exempt financial supplies under the VAGST Act 2008, not taxable supplies, and therefore remain outside VAGST whether characterized as exempt or zero-rated; income derived by the IC from non-resident borrowers is foreign-source and is not subject to Samoan income tax, with zero-rating substantiation relevant only to ancillary fee recovery or cross-border goods collateral, if any.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (electronic departure/cargo declaration lodged with the Ministry for Revenue)
Bill of Lading or Master Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and refund claims are subject to audit by the Ministry for Revenue and refunds may be suspended pending verification. A false or fraudulent claim exposes the IC to: (i) retrospective clawback of the net VAGST refunded, together with late-payment interest; (ii) administrative shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall where recklessness or intentional disregard is established; (iii) monetary fines and imprisonment for tax evasion offences under the VAGST Act 2008 and the Tax Administration Act 2016; and (iv) cancellation or suspension of the zero-rating and refund facility. Directors, registered agents, and beneficial owners may be jointly pursued in civil recovery, and the exempt status of the International Company may be withdrawn for non-compliance with the economic substance regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), through the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, administers all foreign exchange operations and capital account transactions. For International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987, direct foreign currency dealings are generally exempt from CBS approval provided no local currency (WST) is raised or used domestically.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a managed float for the Samoan Tala (WST). Current account payments (trade, services, profit remittance) are freely permitted with underlying documentation. Capital account inflows and outflows require CBS approval unless executed strictly in non-resident foreign currency (usually USD) within the IC framework. There are no repatriation taxes or guaranteed conversion rights; profit remittance from domestic operations requires CBS approval and a tax clearance certificate. For ICs dealing only in foreign currency, convertibility is high and capital mobility is unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For domestic commercial exporters, export proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa within 180 days of shipment and surrendered to a licensed bank within 30 days of receipt, converting 100% of the foreign currency into WST. International Companies that do not export physical goods are exempt. For any minimal service exports from the IC (e.g., licensing fees), the sale is invoiced in foreign currency and no surrender is required as long as funds remain outside the WST banking system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) Samoa

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD and WST); Escrow Account for capital injection
Operational Account (WST only; limited foreign currency support)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa does not have an electronic money institution (EMI) licensing framework. Third-party digital wallets (PayPal, Skrill) generally do not support Samoa-based high-risk commercial onboarding. Established fintech payment processers such as Adyen or Checkout.com rarely accept merchant accounts for P2P lending platforms domiciled in Samoa. Therefore, cross-border settlement must rely on correspondent banking via local commercial banks or offshore banking partners. The Central Bank of Samoa has no sandbox for fintech lending; a Money Lenders License under the Money Lenders Act 2014 is required for any credit activity, and only class A banks may issue payment instruments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For all tier-1 banks, at least one Director and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) must appear physically at a bank branch in Apia for an in-person KYC interview. Remote onboarding via video conferencing is not accepted for ICs in the financial lending sector due to elevated money laundering risk. The registered agent in Samoa must also be present to verify corporate good standing. The process typically takes 4-6 weeks from filing to account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (1) valid Money Lenders License issued by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; (2) audited business plan and model showing expected transaction volumes and counterparty jurisdiction; (3) anti-money laundering (AML) compliance manual with customer due diligence (CDD) measures; (4) evidence of transaction monitoring software; (5) proof of registration with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and compliance with the AML/CFT Act 2018.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex Beneficial Ownership through Trusts (typical IC structure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) certified copy of the trust deed and certificate of incumbency from the licensed trust service provider; (2) identification and proof of residential address for all trustees, protectors (if any), and final UBOs; (3) risk assessment memos over source of wealth and source of funds for each beneficial owner; (4) an organizational chart linking the IC to the trust structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-Border Settlement Destinations (borrower payouts to multiple jurisdictions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (1) list of target settlement countries and regulatory compliance mapping for each; (2) borrower eligibility criteria and automated underwriting algorithm explanation (avoiding black-box concerns); (3) a lawful basis document under applicable data protection law for sharing borrower information; (4) a clearing agreement with a licensed correspondent bank ensuring all outbound wires bear proper purpose codes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No Physical Trading Office in Samoa for lending operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute: (1) physical registered office and resident agent appointment under International Companies Act 1987; (2) signed acknowledgement of the bank's 'virtual business' policy; (3) evidence of a dedicated AML officer based in Apia; (4) guidelines on how loan disbursements avoid financing prohibited sectors (gaming, terrorism, etc.).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or shareholder loan capital from the parent or investors must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 with clear purpose codes: for equity injection use 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital / IS3' under BOP; for intercompany loans use 'Other Investment – Loans – Non-Repayable / IS7'. Supporting documents shall include the IC's board resolution approving the capital injection, capital contribution agreement, source-of-funds evidence from the remitting bank, and a valid security/escrow account instruction at the receiving Samoan bank. No CBS approvall is required for foreign currency remittances to a non-resident IC account held entirely in USD, provided no WST is exchanged.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For loan disbursements to micro-borrowers across the Pacific and global markets, the primary clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 direct debit instruction from the IC's USD operational account to the beneficiary's local bank. For domestic Samoan borrowers, dollar amounts are converted to WST at prevailing rates and settled through the Samoa Automated Clearing House (ACH) operated by the Central Bank of Samoa. For wallet-based payouts (mobile money, e-wallets), a licensed payment aggregator in the beneficiary country is used, channeling funds through a pooling account at a correspondent bank. Trade-related payments (e.g., loan principal repayments) are credited via MT103 with purpose code 'Payment for Service / Interest on Loan' (ISIC/BoP code 'External Income on Loans' or 'Services'). Settlement of inbound loan repayments from foreign borrowers shall be matched daily against the IC's loan ledger to ensure no surplus is trapped in non-resident accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (USD/WST/EUR) transacted with ANZ Samoa or BSP Samoa, with a maximum tenors of 12 months and delivery-backed against a physical lending pipeline.
Cross-currency swaps (limited counterparties; only via offshore investment banks when underlying exposure exceeds USD 5 million, subject to CBS notification if WST leg is involved).
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST via CBS-approved offshore correspondents, permitted only for hedging anticipated loan repayments and not for speculative positions; settled in USD.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Licence Fee Payment (Government Renewal Fee) under the International Companies Act 1987 and the International Companies (Fees) Regulations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year for an existing International Company; a newly incorporated International Company pays a pro-rated first annual fee covering the period to 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-payment penalty equal to 10% of the annual fee applies after 1 July, an additional 10% after 1 October; failure to pay by 31 December is an offence and the company may be struck-off with restoration costs on top.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return containing the registered office, registered agent, directors, members, share capital and the date of any share transfer during the year (Form AAR/IC).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual licence fee, due on or before 30 June of each calendar year; for a newly incorporated company no later than 30 June of the year following incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a daily/default penalty per the Fees Regulations and each director is liable to a fine; continued default beyond 12 months is ground for withdrawal of the registered agent and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (Register of Beneficial Owners and control-chain declaration).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (AML/CFT supervisory record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due on or before 30 June; any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers, must be updated in the statutory register and reported within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is a strict-liability offence under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2019; penalties per day up to USD 10,000 plus personal liability of directors, and the Registrar may suspend the company's licence and initiate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements of the licensed P2P micro-lending entity (annual statutory audit report).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies and Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) as licensing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the financial year end (financial year end commonly 31 December unless the registered agent approves an alternative).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late lodgement is a contravention of the licence and the International Companies Act; may result in monetary penalty, suspension or revocation of the financial services licence, and audit-directed inquiry by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Declaration / Compliance Certificate confirming that the statutory registers, registered office and accounting records remain physically available in Samoa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Delivered by the registered agent no later than 30 June of each year in support of the Annual Return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver the agent's declaration invalidates the continued sponsorship of the International Company; the agent is obliged to resign, and the company will be struck-off if no replacement agent is appointed within 90 days.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An International Company must appoint approved auditors and present audited financial statements if it holds a financial-services or P2P lending licence, or if its gross revenue from regulated lending exceeds USD 1 million in a financial year; otherwise, audit is not mandatory but may be required by a shareholder or shareholders holding at least 10% of the paid-up share capital or by a Registrar's direction.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; no local GAAP modification is available for International Companies. The licensed micro-lending entity must apply IFRS 9 for expected credit loss provisioning on the micro-loan portfolio.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must keep a distinct Register of Beneficial Owners at its registered office in Samoa and each year, on or before 30 June, file an annual confirmation naming every individual who directly or indirectly holds 25% or more of shares, voting power or board-appointment control. Every share transfer during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in a UBO update notice within 14 days; failure to update invalidates transfer warranties under the company's memorandum.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 - US$2,800 per year for a licensed international company registered agent, inclusive of the physical registered office in Samoa and custody of statutory registers.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 - US$9,000 for the annual IFRS audit performed by a Samoa-licensed auditor per licensed P2P lending company.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% for International Companies (ICs) under the International Companies Act 2006; resident companies may qualify for investment incentives, including accelerated depreciation and tax holidays of up to 10 years for approved computer/software services or offshore financial services, reducing effective rates to between 5% and 15%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CIT-1), filed via the Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MfR) e-Services portal (efiling.revenue.gov.ws)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); provisional tax instalments are payable quarterly on 30 April, 31 July, 30 September, and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: registered name, Tax Identification Number (TIN), and registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full legal name, TIN (if issued), and the physical Samoan registered address of the IC; if no Samoan TIN exists, obtain one before submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income: all assessable income, including lending interest and platform fees attributable to Samoa-source activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC is assessable only on Samoa-source income; list only income sourced in Samoa. For a fully exempt IC, enter zero and attach the International Companies Act exemption declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: allowable expenses directly incurred in producing assessable income, excluding capital expenses and penalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident ICs, only expenses attributable to Samoa-source income are deductible; maintain supporting invoices and expense schedules in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and tax liability: apply the 27% statutory corporate rate, deduct any tax credits, and state the net tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC claiming the international company exemption, insert '0' in both taxable income and tax payable; this does not remove the obligation to file if the IC has a TIN or derives Samoa-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 1,500 or 10% of the tax due, whichever is greater; an additional penalty of WST 500 for each month or part thereof of continuous default; late payment interest of 1.5% per month on unpaid tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form IC-AR), filed with the Samoa International Companies Office (SICO) through the SICO online registry
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the anniversary of incorporation each year; a 30-day grace period applies before late fees accrue; the annual government licence fee must accompany the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and certificate/registration number as shown on the certificate of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact IC name and registration number issued by the Registrar of International Companies; do not use trade names without adding the registered legal entity name.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa registered office and licensed registered agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the full Samoan street address, P.O. Box, and the name/agent number of the licensed registered agent in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of directors and shareholders, including identification details and shareholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders/directors, provide passport details and overseas addresses; bearer shares are not permitted under Samoa's AML framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government fee and declaration of continuing International Company exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare that the IC qualifies for the tax exemption under the International Companies Act and confirm no Samoan-source commercial activities are being conducted outside the exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fee of WST 100 per month; non-payment of the annual government licence fee leads to automatic removal from the Register and strike-off of the IC; restoration requires a WST 500 reinstatement fee and, in some cases, a court order.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (general rate imposed on dividends paid by a resident Samoa company to a non-resident shareholder); International Companies are statutorily exempt, and dividends paid by an IC to non-resident shareholders are payable gross with 0% Samoa withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, a completed Samoa Form WHT-TR (Treaty Rate Claim) declaring ultimate beneficial ownership, and evidence that no permanent establishment exists in Samoa. The payer must retain these forms and file a withholding tax return with the MfR; treaty rates under Samoa's DTAs with Australia and New Zealand may reduce dividend WHT to 0–5% for substantial shareholdings, with all claims subject to anti-abuse review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 10% for interest and 10% for royalties paid to non-residents. Under applicable DTAs, interest and royalty rates may be reduced to 0–10%; however, Samoa does not impose withholding tax on interest or royalties paid by an International Company by reason of its statutory exemption. Treaty relief always requires a TRC and completed Form WHT-TR before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 1,000,000 (Samoa tala) aggregate related-party transactions per income year for mandatory Local File; Master File required when the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds WST 5,000,000. Transactions below WST 1,000,000 must still be documented and priced at arm's length.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to International Companies carrying on a relevant activity, including lending/banking, financing and leasing, fund management, and holding company operations. A P2P micro-lending platform must demonstrate core income-generating activities in Samoa: a physical local office, qualified local employees, board meetings held in Samoa, and operating expenditure proportionate to the income generated. An annual economic substance declaration is mandatory with SICO; failure to satisfy the test nullifies the tax exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a tax-exempt Samoa International Company to conceal lending income generated by actual onshore micro-loan operations, or to artificially divert interest revenue to Samoa while management and decision-making remain in a high-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Samoa Income Tax Act (as amended): shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the evaded tax, plus interest at 1.5% per month; criminal conviction may lead to a fine of WST 20,000 and imprisonment for up to seven years; the tax authority may reopen assessments for up to ten years in fraud cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign a false tax return or cause the company to participate in a sham structure are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall; Samoa courts may issue civil restoration orders, asset forfeiture, travel bans, and impose imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a peer-to-peer micro-lending platform, engaging in consumer lending, or processing money transmissions without a lending licence from the Samoa Central Bank and without AML/CFT registration under the Samoa Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Act 2007.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Central Bank Act and AML Act: administrative fines of up to WST 100,000 per violation and criminal fines on the company of up to WST 1,000,000; the Central Bank may suspend or revoke the licence and the company may be ordered to cease operations with immediate effect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers involved in such unlicensed activity face criminal prosecution, personal fines up to WST 50,000, director disqualification, travel restrictions, and imprisonment for up to five years if the AML breach is shown to be wilful or reckless.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pure shell IC with no physical Samoan office, no local directors or employees, no board meetings held in Samoa, and no substantive lending-management functions in Samoa while still claiming the tax exemption and categorising the business as an offshore lending activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance Regulations (Samoa): first-default penalty of WST 10,000; continuing default penalty of WST 5,000 per month; the Registrar may strike off the company and refer the case to the MfR for reversal of tax-exempt status and retrospective taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for inaccurate or false economic substance declarations; the court may impose restitution of the entire tax liability, disqualify the director for up to ten years, issue a travel ban, and in fraud cases sentence imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Nominee directors of a Samoa IC acting solely on telephonic or written instructions of a foreign principal without exercising independent judgement, signing transactions that the constitutional documents prohibit, or failing to maintain proper books and records at the Samoa registered office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Companies Act 2006 and general Samoa companies law: penalty of up to WST 20,000 for misfeasance; the Registrar may strike off the IC for failing to maintain the registered agent or for providing materially false information in the annual return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to restore company assets and account for all secret profits; Samoan courts may impose financial restitution, issue travel bans, disqualify the individual from holding directorship, and on evidence of deception imprison for up to ten years under the Samoa Crimes Act.
